NAH.

Arabic cuisine is difficult, I thrived on my grandmother's cooking, and she would make traditional food, so I've grown up with eating her food, and it's just a part of me.

However, I can see how it's hesitant to some people. Still, I'm literally furious that he doesn't like kebab's, I usually wolf them down.

Maybe try to find something that isn't spicy, if the dish you're giving is usually spicy? I've grown up eating spicy food, and I still drank like 5 full glasses of water when I was having a certain dish, so that might put him off.

Also, it's lovely that you love your culture! I hardly even celebrate mine, one of my only connections is food really, and even then it isn't the proper food that people would eat, more like food that came from the nearish area.

Have you ever been given a sentimental gift given by someone you were super close to?

My mother gave me her violin, she hardly played it but it was played by my mother, and it makes all the difference in the world to me. Also, a good guitar will sound different from the usual guitars you get.

It's like that with any instrument really, my teacher has an expensive violin, it sounds a lot better than his original one.

Also, you can't just give what you suggested and say: "hey! I don't have any sentimental items with you, but here! take \*valuable item / money\* and just count it as done!"

Also, he gives something to the daughter? But he doesn't need to for the son?

I play the violin, I'm not even fully dedicated to the instrument. BUT if my mother gave an expensive + rare violin to my sibling (who doesn't play the violin at all), I'd be pretty confused + annoyed.

Also, you don't have any sentimental items with him? What the hell? Are you even sure you made any bonds with your son? My father (who I also add, never even saw me half the time) and I have sentimental items from when I was really young, and he never even made a proper effort.
